fm.title: Combustion engines
fm.description: Map-based and simple internal-combustion engine models (29 blocks)

rows.intent: Implements a reduced Lundell (claw-pole) alternator and voltage regulator. The back-EMF is proportional to the input speed and field current. The machine operates as a torque source to the combustion engine.

Implements a DC to DC converter supporting bidirectional boost and buck operation. Specify the DC to DC transient response, power limit, and losses. Output voltage tracks the voltage command unless the DC to DC converter is power limiting. Specify electrical losses using measured losses or measured efficiency.

Implements a model for a lithium ion, lithium polymer, or lead acid battery based off of discharge characteristics taken at different temperatures. The model can be parameterized using a typical battery datasheet or through experimental measurement.

Implements a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit battery that you can parameterize using equivalent circuit modeling (ECM). To simulate the state-of-charge (SOC) and terminal voltage, the block uses load current and internal core temperature. Calculates the combined network battery voltage using lookup tables that are functions of the SOC and battery temperature. Use the Estimation Equivalent Circuit Battery block to help create the lookup tables.

Implements a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit battery model that determines the combined voltage of a network battery using parameter lookup tables that are functions of the state-of-charge (SOC). Recommend using the block for estimating battery voltage and SOC, not in system-level models.
Implements an automotive starter as a separately excited DC motor permanent magnet DC motor, or series connection DC motor. The motor operates as a torque source to the combustion engine.

Implements a rotating shaft connected to engine boost components. Uses compressor, turbine, and external torques to calculate the drive shaft speed. Specify one of the following configurations: - Turbocharger: Connect compressor to turbine (external torque optional) - Compressor only: Connect to compressor and provide external torque - Turbine only: Connect to turbine and provide external load torque

Implements a turbocharger or supercharger compressor. Connects to inlet volume, outlet volume, and boost drive shaft. Determines mass and heat flow rates between the volumes and required shaft torque.

Implements a fixed or variable geometry turbine (exhaust side of turbocharger) with a wastegate. Connects to inlet volume, outlet volume, and boost drive shaft. Determines mass and heat flow rates between the volumes and output shaft torque.
Model core engine torque, fuel, and exhaust from lookup maps — use as the map-based heart of a combustion-engine model.

Implements a compression-ignition (CI) engine from intake to exhaust port. Use the block for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) engine control design, or vehicle-level fuel economy and performance simulations. The CI Core Engine block calculates: - Brake torque, using either the torque structure or simple torque model - Fuel flow - Air mass flow, including exhaust gas recirculation (EGR), using a speed-density model - Air-fuel ratio (AFR) - Exhaust temperature and exhaust mass flow rate

Implements a spark-ignition (SI) engine from intake to exhaust port. Use the block in larger vehicle models, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) engine control design, or vehicle-level fuel economy and performance simulations. The SI Core Engine block calculates: - Brake torque, using either the torque structure or simple torque model - Fuel flow - Air mass flow, using either the speed-density or dual-independent cam phasing models - Air-fuel ratio (AFR) - Exhaust temperature and exhaust mass flow rate
Implements a constant volume open thermodynamic system with heat transfer. Uses conservation of mass and energy, assuming an ideal gas, to determine the pressure and temperature.
Implements flow boundary conditions. Set pressure and temperature as constants or external inputs.

Implements isentropic ideal gas flow through an orifice. Uses conservation of mass and energy to determine the mass and heat flow rates. Flow velocity is limited by the local acoustic velocity (choked flow). You can specify a constant, external input, or throttle body geometry orifice area model.

Implements heat exchanger (e.g. intercooler or EGR cooler). Inlet connects to an engine flow component (flow restriction, compressor, turbine, or engine) and outlet connects to a volume (control volume or environment). Model determines heat transfer rate and downstream temperature based on the upstream temperature, effectiveness, and temperature of the cooling medium. Model assumes no pressure drop. Pressure losses can be modeled by the connected flow component.

Implements a compression-ignition (CI) controller that uses the driver torque request to calculate the open-loop commands for injector pulse-width, VGT rack position, and EGR valve area percent required to meet the driver demand. The CI Core Engine block requires the open-loop control commands from the CI Controller block. The block has two subsystems: - Controller: Determines the open-loop CI engine actuator commands based on the torque request and measured engine speed. - Estimator: Determines the torque, estimated air mass flow, exhaust gas recirculation mass flow, exhaust back pressure, and exhaust gas temperature from intake manifold gas pressure, intake manifold gas temperature, engine speed, exhaust gas recirculation valve area percent, variable geometry turbocharger rack position, and variable geometry turbocharger speed. You can specify the torque estimation model.

Implements a spark-ignition (SI) controller that uses the driver torque request in conjunction with measured engine speed to calculate the open-loop air, fuel, spark, and cam-phaser actuator commands required to meet the driver torque demand. The SI Core Engine block requires the actuator commands from the SI Controller block outputs. The block has two subsystems: - Controller: Determines the open-loop commands based on the commanded torque, measured engine speed, and estimated cylinder air mass. - Estimator: Determines the estimated air mass flow, torque, and exhaust gas temperature. You can specify the air mass flow and torque estimation models.
Model a compression-ignition (diesel) engine from lookup maps — use for map-based diesel powertrain simulation.
Model a spark-ignition (gasoline) engine from lookup maps — use for map-based gasoline powertrain simulation.
Model an engine with a simple torque-speed characteristic — use for lightweight powertrain studies without detailed maps.

Implements an internal torque-based, field-oriented controller for an induction motor (IM) with an optional outer-loop speed controller. The torque control implements a strategy for weakening the magnetic flux.

Implements a torque-based, field-oriented controller for an internal permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) with an optional outer-loop speed controller. The torque control implements strategies for maximizing the torque per amp (MTPA) and weakening the magnetic flux.

Implements a torque-based, field-oriented controller for an surface mount permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with an optional outer-loop speed controller. The torque control utilizes quadrature current and does not weaken the magnetic flux.

Implements an equivalent consumption minimization strategy (ECMS) for hybrid electric vehicle control. ECMS optimizes the torque split between the engine and motor to minimize the energy consumption while maintaining the battery state of charge (SOC). Configure the block for different motor locations, adaptive or non-adaptive control, and gear optimization.

Implements a three-part torque converter consisting of an impeller, turbine, and stator with an optional clutch lock-up capability. You can specify the torque converter characteristics and clutch lock-up configurations.
Automated manual transmission (AMT) controller, which generates an open loop clutch command based on a requested gear number.
Implements a pushbelt continuously variable transmission (CVT) controller. The block uses standard pulley and geometric equations to calculate primary and secondary variator positions.
Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT) controller, which generates open loop clutch commands based on a requested gear number.

fm.title: Drivetrain
fm.description: Couplings, differentials, transfer cases, and wheels (14 blocks)

rows.intent: Model a fixed-ratio gearbox with inertia and efficiency losses — use to represent a gear reduction in a driveline.
Model a motorcycle final-drive chain with ratio and compliance — use to couple the transmission to the rear wheel.
Add lumped rotational inertia (with optional damping) to a driveline shaft — use to represent spinning mass.
Model a torsionally-compliant coupling that splits torque between two paths — use for driveline branching with shaft flexibility.
Model shaft torsional compliance (spring/damper) between two rotational ports — use to capture driveline flexibility and resonance.
Implements an idealized dry friction clutch.
Implements an ideal planetary gear coupling consisting of a rigidly coupled sun, ring and carrier. Torque inputs are provided in order to produce the corresponding velocity response.
Model a limited-slip differential that biases torque toward the higher-traction wheel — use for driveline traction studies.
Model an open differential splitting torque equally to two outputs — use as a standard axle differential in a driveline.
Split driveline torque between front and rear axles — use to model 4WD/AWD power distribution.
Model a longitudinal wheel with tire-slip dynamics and a disc brake — use for braking and traction studies with disc braking.
Model a longitudinal wheel with tire-slip dynamics and a drum brake — use for braking and traction studies with drum braking.
Model a longitudinal wheel with tire-slip dynamics and a table-mapped brake — use when brake torque is characterized by data.
Model a longitudinal wheel with tire-slip dynamics and no brake — use for driven or rolling wheels without braking.

fm.title: Electric propulsion
fm.description: Electric motors, inverters, and motor controllers (7 blocks)

rows.intent: Field-oriented controller for a flux-based permanent-magnet motor — use to command torque/current in a flux-based PMSM drive.
Model a permanent-magnet synchronous motor from flux-linkage maps — use for high-fidelity PMSM simulation that captures saturation.
Model a three-phase induction machine with electrical and mechanical dynamics — use as an ACIM traction motor.
Model an interior-permanent-magnet synchronous motor with saliency and reluctance torque — use for IPMSM traction drives.
Model an electric motor and inverter from efficiency/torque maps — use for fast system-level EV powertrain studies.
Model a surface-mount permanent-magnet synchronous motor — use for SPMSM traction and drive simulation.
Model a three-phase voltage-source inverter driving a motor — use to convert DC-bus voltage to AC phase voltages.

fm.title: Scenario
fm.description: Drive-cycle and driver models for closed-loop runs (2 blocks)

rows.intent: Output a standard or custom drive-cycle speed reference versus time — use to drive powertrain and fuel-economy simulations.
Model a driver that produces accelerator and brake commands to track a speed reference — use to close the loop on a drive cycle.
Model an automated manual transmission with clutch and gear-shift logic — use for AMT driveline studies.
Model a CVT with a continuously variable gear ratio — use for CVT powertrain simulation.
Model a dual-clutch transmission with two clutches for seamless shifts — use for DCT driveline studies.
Model an idealized multi-speed transmission with instantaneous gear selection — use for lightweight transmission studies.

fm.title: Utilities
fm.description: Power accounting and Simscape interface helpers (3 blocks)

rows.intent: Bundle component power and energy signals into a power-accounting bus — use to track energy flow for efficiency analysis.
Bridge a Simscape physical two-way connection into a Powertrain Blockset signal interface — use to link physical and signal domains.
Expose a physical connection port on a Powertrain subsystem — use to create a physical pin on a masked subsystem.

fm.title: Vehicle dynamics
fm.description: Longitudinal vehicle body and road-load dynamics (4 blocks)

rows.intent: Model in-plane longitudinal motorcycle body dynamics — use for motorcycle acceleration and braking studies.
Model longitudinal vehicle motion with a single degree of freedom — use for simple straight-line acceleration/braking studies.
Model vehicle longitudinal, vertical, and pitch dynamics (3 DOF) — use for ride and load-transfer studies in the longitudinal plane.
Compute total road load (aerodynamic drag, rolling resistance, grade) opposing motion — use to apply resistive forces in a longitudinal model.
